summary: A placeholder in the shape of content that is loading, so the layout does not jump when the data arrives.
whenToUse: First load of a list, table, card or detail panel whose shape you know.
Mirror the real layout: a circle for an avatar, short lines for names, a block for a preview.
Pair with aria-busy="true" on the region and a visually hidden "Loading tokens".
whenNotToUse: Inside a button or after a click on a control: use Button loading or Spinner.
Long tasks with known progress: use Progress.
When loading takes under about 300 ms: show nothing, the flash is worse than the wait.

dos.title: Match the shape of the real content
dos.text: The page settles in place instead of reflowing when data lands.

donts.title: A whole page of shimmering blocks
donts.text: Load the frame (navigation, titles) for real and use skeletons only where the data goes.

accessibility: Skeletons are always aria-hidden: they are decoration, not content.
Put aria-busy="true" on the loading region and a VisuallyHidden label like "Loading tokens"; remove both when the content arrives.
The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion; use static for long lists.
contentGuidelines: The hidden loading label names the content: "Loading tokens", not "Loading...".
